name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Vagal Interrupt Clamp
description:
The Vagal Interrupt Clamp is a precision neuroelectrical field instrument designed to apply targeted, calibrated electrical stimulation to the vagus nerve, enabling emergency management of life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, neurogenic shock, and severe autonomic storms — particularly those triggered by cyberware cascade failures or electrostimulant overdose. The device resembles a modified clamp or forceps approximately 20cm in length, with two paddle-contact ends lined with conductive polymer. It is applied externally to the neck at the carotid triangle, where the vagus nerve runs closest to the skin surface, and delivers a precise sub-threshold electrical signal that modulates nerve activity without causing tissue damage.

Zheng-Dao's engineering philosophy is evident in the device's control interface: a single dial with five positions (Suppress / Moderate Suppress / Neutral Monitor / Moderate Stimulate / Stimulate) and a numerical readout showing real-time heart rate and estimated vagal tone. There are no automated modes. Zheng-Dao's bioelectrical division believes that in the critical moments of a cardiac or autonomic emergency, a trained operator making active decisions produces better outcomes than an automated protocol that cannot account for the full clinical picture. The clamp's signal generator is powered by a rechargeable cell good for approximately four hours of continuous use, and the conductive polymer contacts are replaced per-use via a simple swap cartridge.

It is called 'The Undertaker's Thumb' in field medicine circles — a reference to the ancient practice of pressing the carotid to check for life, and a sardonic acknowledgment that the device occupies the boundary between intervention and acceptance.
base_technologies: Real-time heart rate and vagal tone monitoring

specifications.monitoring_output: Heart rate (BPM), estimated vagal tone index
specifications.operator_training_requirement: Field Surgical Certification Level 2 or Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Certification

tactical_use: Deployed in response to ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, neurogenic shock, or autonomic storms — particularly the cascade failures that occur when high-integration cyberware loses power suddenly or receives conflicting signals. The operator locates the carotid triangle by palpation, applies the paddle contacts firmly, and begins at Moderate Suppress, adjusting based on the digital readout. In cardiac emergencies, the Clamp is often used as a bridge measure while a defibrillation-capable device is sourced. In autonomic storm cases resulting from cyberware failure, it can be the primary and only intervention needed.
cultural_context: The Vagal Interrupt Clamp has an unusual reputation in GLMZ's medical underground: it is considered both highly legitimate and faintly transgressive, because its mechanism — directly modulating the nervous system's master regulatory nerve — feels to many people like it should not be possible with a handheld device. Among heavily cybered individuals, who face the highest risk of autonomic cascade events, the Clamp is regarded with a complex mixture of relief and unease. Having one present in a crew is considered responsible preparation. Needing it used on you is considered a reminder of how dependent your biology has become on systems that can fail. There are also documented cases of the Clamp being used non-medically to produce altered states, which Zheng-Dao's legal department addresses with consistent grimness.

High-integration cyberware users and their support crews
Underground cyberware surgeons managing post-installation complications
Mercenary medics operating in environments with high cyberware density
story_hooks: A Vagal Interrupt Clamp has been found at a crime scene with the signal dial bypassed and locked at maximum Stimulate — used not to stabilize a patient but to induce cardiac arrest in a way that leaves no conventional forensic trace.

A heavily cybered fixer has been having escalating autonomic storms and is burning through contact cartridges at an unsustainable rate — their cyberware is failing in a way that no one can diagnose, and the Clamp is the only thing keeping them functional.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has released a mandatory firmware update for the Clamp's monitoring system — but operators who've installed it report the readouts have begun displaying a third metric no one can identify, and it sometimes reads values that don't correspond to the patient at all.

A black-market modification for the Clamp allows it to interface directly with certain neural cyberware models, producing a controllable euphoric dissociation — the modification is spreading through the high-integration community, and the line between medical use and recreational use is dissolving.

physical_description.visual_profile: A surgical precision instrument resembling heavy-duty forceps or a calibrated clamp, with a clinical yet utilitarian aesthetic. The device tapers from a control housing at the grip to two flat, paddle-shaped contact arms that curve slightly inward. The overall impression is of a tool engineered for delicate, high-stakes intervention—purposeful and unadorned.
physical_description.dimensions: 21 cm in length; approximately 4 cm wide at the paddle contacts; grip diameter ~1.8 cm. Handheld, single-operator device.
physical_description.weight_description: 340g; substantial enough to feel solid and controlled in the hand, but not burdensome. Requires firm grip during application but portable for emergency medical kits.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade brushed titanium alloy housing; grip sleeve in matte black polymer composite for thermal and electrical isolation.
physical_description.finish: Satin-brushed metallic body with minimal reflectivity; non-skid textured grip zone. Contact paddles have a faint iridescent sheen from the biocompatible conductive polymer coating (easily replaced). Minimal chrome detailing at hinge points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant titanium silver-gray with matte black grip sections. Accent color: clinical white on the contact paddles and control housing. Digital readout backlit in cool cyan-blue. Single warning LED in amber near the power indicator.
physical_description.interface_elements: A five-position rotary dial (Suppress / Moderate Suppress / Neutral Monitor / Moderate Stimulate / Stimulate) with tactile detents and printed markings. Small digital LCD readout (approximately 2 x 1.5 cm) displaying real-time heart rate (BPM) in white numerals and a vagal tone index bar graph. Power indicator light (green during operation, amber during low-battery). A narrow cartridge bay on the underside for quick-swap conductive polymer contact pads. No buttons; all control is through dial and tactile feedback.
distinctive_features: Two flat, rounded contact paddles with subtle ridged texture to prevent slip during application to the neck.
Minimalist control dial with no digital buttons or touch surface—purely mechanical, designed for operation with gloved hands or tremoring fingers.
Small cyan-blue backlit LCD display recessed into the control housing, visible from above and at a slight angle.
Single amber LED mounted near the power socket; glows softly during low-battery conditions.
Cartridge bay with a small release button and color-coded polymer contact pads (typically white or translucent) visible on insertion.
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC embossed in clean sans-serif font on the upper control housing. Regulatory stamps: GLMZ Medical Authority approval, TIER 3+ licensing mark, and a small serial number plate. Warning label in white and red on the grip: 'CAROTID APPLICATION ONLY — CERTIFIED OPERATOR REQUIRED.' Manufacturing date code laser-marked on the cartridge bay.
physical_description.condition_typical: Clinical and sterile in appearance; often carried in a padded foam insert within a hard-shell medical case. In active use, the contact paddles may show slight residue from conductive gel or skin contact, but are wiped clean after each procedure. The dial shows minor cosmetic wear from repeated repositioning but no visible damage. Battery indicator is monitored closely between uses.
